findings.issue: New UI (team list, coverage table, toggle buttons, 'Team is full' state) was never viewed: zero browser commands, screenshots or HTTP probes across the whole session; only the Playwright suite and tsc exercised it.
findings.suggestion: After the suite passes, start the app and run agent-browser against /team and /pokemon/pikachu with a populated cookie, and hand-check the full-team and malformed-cookie paths the tests don't cover.

findings.issue: Called the read tool with a bash-style 'command' argument, which failed validation, then fell back to bash cat for the rest of the session.
findings.suggestion: Use the read tool with its path/offset/limit schema; it avoids the error and gives cleaner truncation for large files.

findings.issue: Two failed greps against app/node_modules before realizing dependencies weren't installed.
findings.suggestion: Check whether node_modules exists (or just run npm install) before grepping package internals.

findings.issue: Edit submitted with a literal placeholder 'x' as oldText, guaranteeing a miss; one wasted call.
findings.suggestion: Always paste the real anchor text from the file when issuing an edit.

findings.issue: Nearly all source reading was done via bash cat with whole-file dumps, contrary to the harness's read-tool guidance, and it caused the one arg-validation error.
findings.suggestion: Prefer read for file examination; reserve bash for grep/find-style searches.

findings.issue: sanitizeTeam defensively handles malformed, duplicate and oversized cookies, but none of those paths was ever verified (no test covers them and no manual probe was made).
findings.suggestion: Add a quick manual or scripted check of a >6-entry and a garbage cookie against /team and /pokemon/:name.

summary: An unusually disciplined 35-turn session: full requirements and framework-API reconnaissance before the first edit, one deliberate architectural decision (cookie-backed team state) that pre-empted the likeliest failure, and a first-pass 63/63 test run with zero fix cycles. Weaknesses are confined to a handful of cheap tool errors and, more notably, verification that stopped at the test suite plus a typecheck — the brand-new team UI was never once looked at in a browser or probed beyond what Playwright checks.
